verdict.rationale: Context.dev documents schema-driven extraction: it reads relevant pages from a URL and returns an object matching your JSON Schema, with no selectors needed. It also has an Answers endpoint that takes a natural-language question or task and returns JSON with sources. However, the evidence never says the page-extraction endpoint accepts free-text natural-language instructions, and Answers is live-web research rather than extraction from a specific page. missing for 10: explicit natural-language prompt/instruction parameter for page extraction, examples of instruction-driven extraction, independent or hands-on corroboration of extraction quality

support.subject: As a developer, I can extract structured data from a page using natural language instructions instead of writing selectors

citations.quote: Start from a URL, read relevant pages, and return data shaped by your JSON Schema.
Crawl relevant pages and return an object that matches your JSON Schema, with controls for grounding, coverage, and freshness.
Research a question or task on the live web and return JSON with source URLs.
